title: Xenogears (PS1) in a Godot shell with AI-redrawn HD sprites — code and art made almost entirely by AI under my direction, sources included
author: T3hVerm
selftext:
Hi all. I made a fan mod of Xenogears that I wanted for myself for years, and almost all of it was done by AI while I directed and checked the results. I'm sharing everything, including the pipeline.

**What it is:**

- the game runs in a Godot 4 shell on top of the open-source Weltall core (a C++ bridge feeds each frame's geometry and sprites into Godot), with modern lighting and widescreen
- every character sprite redrawn in HD with image models
- I played the whole game through in it, both discs

**How AI was used:**

- code: Claude Code wrote the bridge, the Godot shell and all the tools; one model planned and verified, another did the bulk work
- sprites: extracted from the game, redrawn with Gemini and a custom-trained LoRA from reference sheets, then cut back into the game's sprite cells automatically
- checking: automated sweeps over all 730 maps to find what is still drawn in original pixels, plus an in-game "frame report" key to capture defects

**What it is not:** it's not the game. No disc images or game files are included, you need your own.

**Videos:**

- all 34 Deathblows of Fei, Citan and Emeralda: https://youtu.be/cxWjZwgbCas
- a walk around Kislev, NPCs in HD: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ez5WRn55g5s

Sources, sprite pipeline and build instructions (MIT): https://github.com/Vermili0n/xenogears-hd

Honest notes: some sprites are still missing or rough. It's good enough for me, so I'm not planning to polish it further. If you have ideas on how to make it better — take it and do it.

Huge thanks to the author of Weltall — without that core none of this would exist.

comments.author: Charlemagneffxiv
comments.body: Hey I dig it. I actually think I saw your videos on YT about a week ago when I was searching to see if anyone else was making an original Xenogears like game.

replies.author: T3hVerm
replies.body: Thanks! Could be — I posted a couple of videos back when I was doing this for the RetroArch emulator, probably a couple of weeks ago.
